note.happening: Netflix fell 2.25% to close at 60.75. That is below the 61.14–61.64 zone, which the data now lists as resistance (a ceiling) rather than support (a floor), and no support level appears below the price. The only news is a confirmed Netflix animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-19.
note.business: The business itself is still strong. Revenue over the last twelve months was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, rose to 11.4B from 9.0B. Operating margin, the share of sales kept as operating profit, improved to 31.3% from 29.14%. The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each share owns a bit more of the company. What is at risk is the pace. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters earlier. Analysts cut their estimate for this quarter's earnings per share by 7.3% in 30 days, to 0.68. The filings also say the 31% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like that usually fade. The balance sheet is not a pressing worry: debt of 12.7B against cash of 8.2B leaves net debt of 4.4B, which is small next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. The animated-series news is about content and mood. It does not change demand, margins or cash in any way the data can show. Segment data is not available.

worth.text: At 60.75, the discounted cash flow model (a DCF, which values today's estimate of all future cash) says the market expects free cash flow to start growing at about 13.7% a year, using a 10.1% discount rate. If starting growth is 10%, the value is 52.3. If it is 20%, the value is 77.98. The model's middle case is 64.3, with a bear case of 37.83 and a bull case of 76.88. Measured against its own history, the stock looks much cheaper. Its price-to-sales ratio of 5.0 sits at the 23rd percentile of its own 5-year range and below the peer median of 7.3, which puts the own-history value between 60.37 and 122.15, with a midpoint of 84.5. The gap between the two methods comes down to one question: does Netflix still deserve the multiples it earned when it grew faster? The earnings multiples are modest, at 17.3 times trailing earnings and 16.1 times next year's. Margin is the main thing that could pull the value down: if operating margin fell to 23%, the value would be 58.22, and at 15% it would be 38.45.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing somewhere between 10% and 20% a year, close to the 13.7% the price implies, even though quarterly sales growth has slowed to 11.85%.
